comment: The revert-check of `tools/check-gate-coverage.sh` (issue #943): one mutation per invariant — the refusal of a path no glob names, the refusal of an allowlist entry that states no reason, the count the verdict prints, and the first-step wiring in the profile that makes the check owed at all. Run it with `bash tools/mutate.sh --mutations tools/tests/check-gate-coverage-mutations.json`; `.pi/skills/revert-check` owns the rule and `.pi/skills/mutation-runner` owns how. `case-cmd` runs one named case (`--case {case}`), so a mutation pays one case and not the suite; the wiring record names the profile and the case that reads the plan, because a check nobody owes is a check that never runs. The search is a single line and unique in its file, because the runner's replacement is literal and line-based, and the file is restored byte for byte afterwards.

mutations.label: unnamed-path-refused
mutations.why: a tracked path no glob names and no allowlist entry explains is the finding, so a check that reports the count and passes is a green gate over a path nothing measures

mutations.label: allowlist-entry-states-a-reason
mutations.why: an allowlist entry that states no reason is refused, because an entry with no reason is the silence the check exists to end

mutations.label: verdict-carries-the-count
mutations.why: the verdict carries what it counted, so an allowlisted path and a named one are told apart instead of both reading as covered

mutations.label: the-check-is-owed-for-any-path
mutations.why: the check's condition is the whole file set against the profile's globs, which no path names, so a profile that leaves it behind a narrow glob runs it for nobody
